translations.answer: Maintainers did not use atomic flag migration for publishing, but required the use of realtime_tools already existing priority-inheritance recursive mutex. PR #3197 migrated controllers_lock_ and all call sites to realtime_tools::prio_inherit_recursive_mutex, with Windows retaining std::recursive_mutex. The PR has been reviewed and tested. It addresses the source code-level priority inversion risk and should not be expressed as having quantified jitter improvement.
translations.applicability: The ros2_control controller_manager uses the POSIX controllers_lock_ on platforms; Windows uses a standard mutex fallback.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict, and there is formal documentation or precise independent replication.
translations.details.attempts.0: The initial PoC used atomic flag migration for RT→non-RT triggering; maintainers opted for a smaller scope PI recursive mutex replacement.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Tracing from SCHED_FIFO update() to publish_activity(), and checking if controllers_lock_ is held by the executor/service path.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: PR #3197 migrated controllers_lock_ to realtime_tools::prio_inherit_recursive_mutex and retained the Windows fallback.
translations.details.environments.0: The issue was discovered in ros2_control master commit a03be840; the PR was validated in ROS 2 Rolling build; POSIX uses realtime_tools PI mutex, Windows falls back to std::recursive_mutex.
translations.details.limits.0: The merged code proof of concept was accepted, but it does not prove that the original path had measurable jitter or provide performance improvement numbers.
translations.details.limits.1: The Windows fallback path does not use a PI mutex, and the applicability is different.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The PR received two maintainers' approvals, and the changes were tested and merged.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: How should the priority inversion risk be mitigated when the RT update path and non-RT services share a recursive mutex?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: The mutex replacement should still be measured in fallback, service concurrency, and controller switch pressure scenarios for worst-case delay.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The standard recursive mutex does not provide the required priority inheritance, and low-priority threads holding the lock may block RT threads.
translations.details.symptoms.0: This is a potential priority inversion/jitter risk identified during code audit, with no thread showing robot-specific real-time performance or benchmarking.
translations.source.title: Real-time path sharing recursive mutex in ros2_control is replaced with priority-inheritance mutex
translations.terms.1: Priority-inheritance mutex (优先级继承互斥锁)
translations.title: What is the final mitigation for the RT path sharing recursive mutex in publish_activity?
